thread:
sasha: Hey team — I pushed MICA-7B weights to s3://redwood-models/mica/mica-7b/v1/ and added a minimal tokenizer to the same prefix. Quick sanity check before we add it to the catalog?

kevin: Thanks — can you paste the exact tokenizer files? we had a tokenizer-vocab mismatch last time.

sasha: sure: s3://redwood-models/mica/mica-7b/v1/tokenizer.json and tokenizer.vocab. Note the vocab size is 50288.

olivia: heads up — the original repo uses a fallback unk token <unk> but our tokenizer.json declares <unk> as '<UNK>' (case diff). that breaks our normalization pipeline. :eyes:

mahmoud: ugh. that's the same class of bug we saw with tessera. we should add a small wrapper mapping tokens to our canonical -> '<unk>' during load. I can PR a loader that normalizes case.

sasha: cool. i'll patch the tokenizer in the s3 prefix but want to run perf tests before certifying. kicked off a smoke bench with bench-bot — command:
```
bench-bot run --model s3://redwood-models/mica/mica-7b/v1 --conf tests/latency_smoke.yaml 
# conf: batch_sizes: [1,4,8], seq_len: [64,256], runs: 10
```

bench-bot: perf run started (id: mica-7b-smoke-2026-03-17-01) — will post metrics when done.

bench-bot: perf run finished — summary:
```
model: mica-7b v1
batch=1  p50=28ms  p95=62ms  tokens/sec=480
batch=4  p50=42ms  p95=120ms tokens/sec=1800
batch=8  p50=85ms  p95=240ms tokens/sec=3300
notes: GPU mem ~13.2GB (using int8), kv_cache enabled
```

kevin: p50 numbers look reasonable. p95 at batch=8 is high — likely queuing at the batching layer. what's our dynamic_batching window?

sasha: default window is 20ms, max_batch_delay=50ms in the serving config. i tested with that.

olivia: can we try two quick variations: (A) max_batch_delay=10ms (more latency focused), (B) disable dynamic batching and prepack a fixed batch of 4 to see throughput/latency tradeoff?

mahmoud: i'll queue both. running:
```
bench-bot run --model s3://redwood-models/mica/mica-7b/v1 --conf tests/latency_variants.yaml --overrides '{"dynamic_batching":{"max_batch_delay_ms":10}}'
bench-bot run --model s3://redwood-models/mica/mica-7b/v1 --conf tests/latency_variants.yaml --overrides '{"dynamic_batching":{"enabled":false},"fixed_batch_size":4}'
```

bench-bot: variant run A finished:
```
batch=1  p50=29ms  p95=58ms
batch=4  p50=39ms  p95=85ms
batch=8  p50=78ms  p95=150ms
notes: reduced p95 at batch=4, throughput slightly down
```

bench-bot: variant run B (fixed batch 4) finished:
```
batch=4  p50=35ms  p95=70ms  tokens/sec=1600
notes: lower variance, more predictable latency, less peak throughput than dynamic batching at batch=8
```

kevin: nice. that suggests default dynamic batching helps throughput but increases tail latency at high batch sizes. for catalog entry we should default to dynamic batching with recommended max_batch_delay=10ms for latency-sensitive customers. document both options in onboarding notes.

olivia: agree. also — add tokenizer normalization note and include a quick loader snippet in the repo.

sasha: will do PRs: (1) tokenizer fix + loader shim, (2) onboarding doc with perf summary + recommended serving config (dynamic_batching max 10ms, default batch policy: prefer 4-8 token batches), (3) unit check that rejects tokenizer case mismatch.

mahmoud: ping me on the PR for the loader — i'll validate the quant path.

kevin: small ask — can bench-bot attach the raw logs and perf traces to the run id? makes it easier to paste into the catalog page.

bench-bot: done — uploaded artifacts to s3://redwood-logs/bench/mica-7b/mica-7b-smoke-2026-03-17-01.tar.gz and variant runs under mica-7b-variants-2026-03-17.tar.gz

sasha: great, i'll start the PRs and tag y'all. thanks! :thumbsup:
